summary: First full E2E run of Crypto Conex (backend + CRM + public connect page). Backend: 26 pytest tests (public, auth/roles 401/403, queue assign/take/reject, session accept/transfer/end, tech isolation, links lifecycle, devices CRUD, technicians CRUD, settings, audit, WS signalling/privacy/chat/command guards, rate limiting); 25/26 pass. One real bug: a technician can rename ANY device (scope-merge bug). Frontend: public page (desktop + 390px mobile), /assistir valid/invalid/revoked, Clerk ticket sign-in for admin/tech1/a Clerk user with no profile, refresh keeps the session, sign-out goes back to /sign-in, dashboard KPIs, Lisbon clock ticking, exact footer text, queue assign dialog + 'Atender eu', viewer accept, full WebRTC (headless getDisplayMedia replaced by a canvas.captureStream() stub, then a real RTCPeerConnection over the backend TURN/ICE: viewer-pc-state=connected and the video receives frames), zoom, side panel, command-console-web, two-way chat, privacy overlay on/request/disable, end -> public-ended, Histórico row with DD/MM/AAAA HH:mm dates, transfer in the Sessions page -> client sees the new technician, tech1 accepts again -> connected, client WS drop -> RealtimeClient reconnects and video continues, Devices search/rename/history/delete/filters, Links create/copy/revoke, Configurações technician add/edit/permissions/active/activity/delete, Sistema save, Auditoria list, technician gets no Configurações nav and a blocked message. CRITICAL bug found in the WebRTC viewer: an endless session:join loop meant WebRTC NEVER reached 'connected' (stuck at 'connecting', 198 'setRemoteDescription wrong state: stable' unhandled rejections, and the Emergent error overlay blocked the client chat). I applied a minimal fix in 2 frontend hooks. After that every viewer flow passed.

critical.issue: Technician scope bypass and wrong-row update: query built as {'id': did, **scope}, and for technicians scope = {'id': {'$in': ids}}, which OVERWRITES the 'id' key. update_one therefore renames the FIRST device in the technician's history, not 'did'. Reproduced: tech2 PATCH on a device it never served -> 200, and a different device got renamed, while support_requests/sessions of 'did' were also renamed (update_many by did runs without any scope check). Fix: q = {'id': did}; if scope: q['$and'] = [scope], or check did in ids -> 404.

minor.issue: client_ip() trusts the FIRST X-Forwarded-For entry, which the client controls. Sending a random X-Forwarded-For header on each request bypasses the 10/min limit entirely (verified: dozens of connects with random XFF, never a 429; same XFF -> 429 after 10). Use the right-most/trusted proxy hop or the ingress real-IP header.

Pending requests from web clients that close the tab without pressing TERMINAR are never expired or auto-cancelled on device disconnect, so the queue fills with stale 'Offline' PENDENTE items (44 pending seen on the dashboard). Consider auto-cancel after a device has been offline for N minutes, or a TTL.
The audit actor for sessao.terminada is the technician NAME ('TEST Técnico Um'), while all other actions use the email. This makes the audit log inconsistent.
Device JWT TTL is 4h. RealtimeClient keeps reusing the same token, so after expiry the reconnects fail forever with 4401. No refresh path exists.

ui_bugs.issue: FIXED BY TESTER (please review): onStatus re-joined whenever session:status had device_connected===true. But the server's reply to session:join is itself a session:status with device_connected:true, so this was an infinite join loop. Each join made the server emit technician:joined, the device recreated its RTCPeerConnection and sent a new offer, and the viewer tore down its pc. WebRTC never connected. Fix applied: ignore the join reply (only re-join when the payload has no 'status' key).

FIXED BY TESTER: the webrtc:answer handler called setRemoteDescription regardless of signalingState, which caused unhandled rejections ('Called in wrong state: stable'). These triggered the Emergent error overlay, and that overlay intercepted clicks on client-chat-send. Added a guard (signalingState === 'have-local-offer') and a catch.

Under React.StrictMode (dev), the effect runs twice. The cleanup runs before api.get('/me') resolves, so client is still undefined and the first RealtimeClient leaks: 2 WebSockets per CRM tab, causing duplicate events and joins. The header briefly showed 'A RELIGAR…' after load. Use a cancelled flag or create the client synchronously.

integration_issues.issue: Remote video arrives at only 320x180 from a 1280x720 source (still the case after ~5s and after reconnect). For screen sharing, consider track.contentHint='detail', degradationPreference='maintain-resolution', and raising maxBitrate on the sender. 'Débito' shows '—' during the first samples.

issues: public-detected-os text (#64748B, ~11px mono) has low contrast on the dark background
Logo emblem.png has a visible dark square background (not transparent) behind the coins
Sonner toasts (top-right) cover the header member name/avatar
Mobile 390px: the nav is a horizontal scroll bar above the logo, and the 'Ate…' item is cut off without any scroll affordance

action_items: Fix PATCH /api/devices/{did} scope merge ({'id': did, **scope} overwrites id): technicians can rename arbitrary or wrong devices

Review and keep the tester's fix in frontend/src/hooks/useViewerRtc.js (join loop) and useDeviceSession.js (answer state guard). Optionally also de-duplicate technician:joined -> startPeer so that multiple joins do not recreate the peer
Harden rate limiting against a spoofed X-Forwarded-For
Auto-expire or cancel stale pending requests from offline web devices
Fix the CrmContext StrictMode leak of RealtimeClient
Minor: consistent audit actor (email), contrast of the detected-OS text
critical_code_review_comments: server.py _device_scope merged into the filter with dict-unpacking: the same pattern must be avoided anywhere a scope dict and an explicit id key coexist
rename_device update_many on support_requests/sessions runs even if the scoped device update matched a different doc
realtime.on_join always replies session:status, and clients must not treat this reply as a 'device reconnected' signal (root cause of the loop)
useDeviceSession: technician:joined always calls startPeer() (closes and recreates the pc), so redundant joins (initial + _state open + session:started) cause renegotiation churn
server.py is 602 lines, close to the 700 limit; consider splitting the routers

success_rate.frontend: ~95% after tester fix (WebRTC viewer was 0% before the fix)

seed_data_creation: Created a Clerk user semperfil+clerk_test@cryptoconex.pt (no CRM profile) for the access-denied test (recorded in test_credentials.md). Test devices/requests/links/technicians use the TEST_ prefix. TEST_ pending requests were cancelled and TEST_OS devices deleted via cleanup_test_data.py. Revoked TEST links and ended sessions remain in history.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Headless screen share: add_init_script overriding navigator.mediaDevices.getDisplayMedia to return canvas.captureStream(15). WebRTC then really connects via the backend ICE/TURN. Sign-in: run clerk_tickets.py, then in the page goto /sign-in, wait for window.Clerk.loaded, and call Clerk.client.signIn.create({strategy:'ticket'}) + setActive (the ?__clerk_ticket URL was flaky). Tickets are single use. Before UI viewer tests, run cleanup_open_sessions.py so that session-open-* .first picks the new session. To simulate a WS drop: wrap window.WebSocket in the init script and close window.__ws.at(-1). Not verified: real OS screen picker, native Android/Windows apps, remote control commands (web clients never grant consent.control; only checked through the WS error path).
rca of the issue: WebRTC stuck at 'connecting': the viewer sends session:join -> the server replies session:status{device_connected:true,status} -> useViewerRtc.onStatus calls join() again -> infinite loop. Each join -> technician:joined to the device -> startPeer() closes the pc and sends a new offer -> the viewer recreates its pc. Answers arrive for stale pcs -> setRemoteDescription in the 'stable' state (198 unhandled rejections) -> the Emergent overlay blocks clicks. Mitigation applied: only re-join on broadcasts without 'status' + an answer signalingState guard. Verified: connected within 1-3s, video frames received, the chat/privacy/end/transfer/reconnect flows all pass.
